pathway.title: NEWELL BRANDS INC. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. Leverage improved on earnings, not repayment. NEWELL BRANDS INC. reports net debt of USD 4,592 million against USD 4,470 million at FY2025, so the fall in net debt to normalized EBITDA from 5.07x to 4.46x comes from trailing-twelve-month normalized EBITDA rising from USD 882 million to USD 1,030 million. That EBITDA is a management measure; it includes tariff recoveries recorded in Q2 2026, and removing the roughly USD 126 million named for that quarter would put net leverage near 5.08x (a one-sided sensitivity, calculated below). On a filing-based EBITDA before impairment the ratio is 5.51x. The issuer reported a GAAP net loss of USD 323 million over the twelve months to Q3 2026. Mechanic: lenders and the market will test sustainability of EBITDA, not the reported ratio. Implication: debt service capacity is thinner than the headline ratio suggests.

2. Cash generation does not cover the obligations ahead of equity. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 53 million over the twelve months to Q3 2026, against net interest expense of USD 341 million and cash dividends of USD 127 million, leaving USD 74 million negative after dividends. First-quarter seasonality and an inventory build explain part of the profile, and Q3 2026 alone was strongly positive, but the year relies on the third and fourth quarters, and receivables factoring and tariff refunds have supported operating cash flow. Implication: refinancing, not internal cash, funds any maturity; the issuer's own full-year operating cash flow outlook of about USD 150 million is a management claim.

3. The capital structure is pushed out but not de-risked. The USD 500 million 2027 notes are gone and the secured revolver was replaced by an asset-based facility of up to USD 800 million, with USD 215 million drawn and USD 480 million of net availability at 2026-09-30. The next large maturity is USD 1,252 million in 2028, which exceeds liquidity of USD 729 million before factoring. Under the facility's terms its maturity springs to 91 days before the earliest material debt maturity if USD 125 million or more is still outstanding, so the 2028 notes can pull the facility's maturity forward (the 2028 notes' exact date is not printed in the pages read). Implication: access to the bond market in 2027 and early 2028 is the decisive event.

4. Priority claims on current assets are growing. The asset-based facility is secured on receivables, inventory, equipment, intellectual property and deposit accounts, and a receivables purchaser holds a first-priority lien on certain unsold receivables. At 2026-09-30 about USD 435 million of receivables were sold across two programs, and borrowing-base availability of USD 741 million means drawn secured borrowings could rise by USD 526 million from USD 215 million. Mechanic: more secured and sold claims on the same current assets reduce the unencumbered pool behind USD 4,626 million of other debt. This is a mechanic, not a recovery conclusion; lien priority between the lenders and the purchaser is not described in the pages read.

5. Business risk is concentrated. Amazon and Walmart supplied about 17% and 13% of FY2025 net sales, the 10-K says retailer power may limit price recovery, Learning and Development earned more than the whole nine-month 2026 segment operating income while Home and Commercial Solutions earned USD 9 million, and a USD 101 million tradename impairment fell in Q3 2026. Implication: a retailer decision or a weak category can move cash flow materially, and impairments signal that asset values already reflect lower expected earnings.

6. Debt-like funding sits outside the debt figure. Factoring of USD 435 million is not in reported debt; the issuer has cut both programs' limits and intends to reduce debt and factoring by a couple of hundred million dollars in 2026. Net debt plus factoring over normalized EBITDA is 4.88x (calculated below). Reducing factoring draws on liquidity unless replaced.

runs.text: Strengths. (1) Brand breadth and reach: the issuer sells in over 150 countries with a portfolio including Rubbermaid, Sharpie, Graco, Coleman and Yankee Candle (Documentary Fact). (2) Earnings momentum: trailing-twelve-month normalized EBITDA rose from USD 882 million at FY2025 to USD 1,030 million at Q3 2026, and management reports two consecutive quarters of sales growth (Documentary Fact for the figures; Management Language for the growth characterisation). (3) Maturity runway: the 2027 notes were redeemed and the asset-based facility runs to 2031 on its stated terms (Documentary Fact). (4) A profitable core: Learning and Development earned a segment operating income of USD 553 million over nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact). (5) Seasonal cash generation: Q3 2026 operating cash flow of USD 297 million, derived from cumulative statements, shows the model produces cash in the second half (Analyst Interpretation). (6) Transparent reporting with net debt and EBITDA reconciliations each quarter (Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. (1) Leverage: net debt to normalized EBITDA of 4.46x, and 5.51x on a filing-based basis before impairment, with GAAP losses over the last twelve months (Documentary Fact and calculation). (2) Thin cash conversion relative to interest and dividends (Documentary Fact and calculation). (3) Customer concentration and weak pricing power (Documentary Fact). (4) A weak largest segment: Home and Commercial Solutions had a segment operating loss of USD 138 million in FY2025 and carries the Q3 2026 impairment, and Outdoor and Recreation lost USD 17 million over nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact). (5) Structural subordination risk through secured borrowing-base debt and sold receivables, and a springing maturity (Analyst Interpretation). (6) Reliance on management measures and one-off tariff refunds in 2026 earnings and cash flow (Documentary Fact). (7) Covenant headroom, ownership and ratings cannot be assessed from the pack (Insufficient Information; not an adverse conclusion).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The transactions in the pack are financings by a listed company with no sponsor, not an acquisition or a sponsor transaction, and all are executed and reported as completed except where marked as a subsequent event. On 2026-07-30 the issuer and a subsidiary borrower, Newell Brands Ireland Services DAC, with certain domestic and foreign subsidiary guarantors, entered a five-year asset-based revolving credit facility led by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. of up to 800, subject to a borrowing base of qualified cash, receivables, inventory, equipment and intellectual property, with an uncommitted accordion of up to 500; 490 was drawn on closing to repay and replace the 1,000 secured Credit Revolver that was due in August 2027. The facility is secured by a lien on deposit accounts, receivables, inventory, equipment and intellectual property, carries a Consolidated Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio test that applies only when borrowings exceed levels relative to capacity, and matures on 2031-07-30 or, if indebtedness of 125 or more is still outstanding 91 days before that debt's own scheduled maturity, on that 91st day before it. In August 2026 the issuer sold 600 of 6.250% senior unsecured notes due 2031 under an indenture dated 2026-08-19, received proceeds of 592, used them to redeem the 6.375% senior notes due 2027 at 101.530% (total consideration about 508) and to repay part of the ABL borrowings, and recorded a loss on extinguishment of 16 in Q3 2026 including 3 of revolver costs. At 2026-09-30, 215 was drawn on the ABL and letters of credit of 46 were issued under it, leaving net availability of about 480 on borrowing-base availability of 741; gross debt was 4,841 and net debt 4,592. The effect on liquidity is a longer runway and a clear 2027, but drawn secured borrowings now sit ahead of the unsecured notes in the same collateral pool as receivables and inventory, and, on the analyst's reading of the springing maturity (Analyst Interpretation), the facility's 2031 date holds only if the 2028 notes are refinanced or repaid in time; the 2028 notes' exact maturity date is not printed in the pages read.

Two receivables financings changed in the quarter and after it. The Customer Receivables Purchase Agreement limit was cut from 700 to 625 effective 2026-09-14, with a first-priority lien granted to the purchaser over certain receivables not sold and a lower funding rate; 300 was outstanding at 2026-09-30. The separate Receivables Facility, with 135 outstanding at 2026-09-30, was renewed effective 2026-10-02 (a subsequent event) to 2027-10-01 with its limit on factored receivables outstanding cut to 75. Management says it expects to reduce total debt and factoring by a couple of hundred million dollars in 2026 and that lower factoring proceeds reduce expected 2026 operating cash flow, now about 150; this is Management Language and is unproven. Earlier financings in the record: in May 2025 the issuer sold 1.25 billion of 8.500% senior notes due 2028 and used the proceeds to redeem its 4.200% notes due 2026 in June 2025, and in 2025 it repaid its 3.900% notes due 2025. No acquisition, divestiture or ownership change occurs in 2026 in the pack; the 2019 sale of The United States Playing Card Company is the source of a pending indemnification claim by the buyers, whose amount is not quantified. Status of sponsor, ownership percentages and use of any proceeds beyond debt refinancing: Insufficient Information.

fields.value: NEWELL BRANDS INC. entered the third quarter of 2026 with higher earnings but unchanged leverage in dollar terms. Net debt, as management defines it, was 4,592 at 2026-09-30 against 4,470 at 2025-12-31, so the improvement in net debt to normalized EBITDA from 5.07x to 4.46x came entirely from trailing-twelve-month normalized EBITDA rising from 882 to 1,030, not from paying debt down. That EBITDA is a management measure that adds back impairments, restructuring and share-based compensation, and it includes pre-tax tariff recoveries recorded in Q2 2026; on GAAP the issuer lost 323 over the twelve months to Q3 2026 after non-cash impairments, and Q3 2026 itself was a net loss of 81 after a 101 tradename impairment. Cash generation is thin: operating cash flow less capital expenditure was 53 over the twelve months to Q3 2026 while cash dividends paid were 127, and FY2025 interest paid in cash of 354 covered by normalized EBITDA only 2.49x. The refinancing in the third quarter replaced the 2027 note maturity and the secured revolver with a 2031 note and a new borrowing-base facility, which removes the near-term wall but leaves the 2028 notes (1,252 on the 2025-12-31 ladder) as the next large maturity, and the new facility can mature ahead of 2031 if material debt is still outstanding 91 days before its maturity. Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is cash of 249 plus net ABL availability of about 480, before factoring, which the issuer says it intends to reduce. The base is usable for a credit snapshot with the limits listed in `## Gaps`.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: NEWELL BRANDS INC. is a widely held, Nasdaq-listed consumer goods group in the execution phase of a multi-year turnaround, with no sponsor, no controlling holder identified in the pack and a business that depends on large retailers: Amazon and Walmart were about 17% and 13% of FY2025 net sales, and the 10-K says retailer bargaining power may limit its ability to recover cost increases through pricing. Profit is concentrated in Learning and Development, while Home and Commercial Solutions, the largest segment by sales, produced a segment operating loss in FY2025 and a small profit over nine months 2026 that includes a 101 tradename impairment in Q3 2026. For creditors the transaction story is a refinancing, not a sponsor event: in July and August 2026 the issuer put in place a new borrowing-base facility of up to 800, issued 600 of 6.250% senior notes due 2031 and redeemed the 6.375% notes due 2027, which removes the 2027 maturity but moves part of the capital structure to a secured facility and leaves the 2028 notes as the next large maturity. The documented behaviour is a refinancing through a new note issue and a redemption above par, a continued quarterly dividend while free cash flow after capital expenditure was negative over nine months 2026, and a stated intention to reduce debt and factoring; no priming, uptier, drop-down or debt-funded distribution appears in the pack, but the executed documents that would show legal capacity are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transactions in the pack are financings by a listed company with no sponsor, not an acquisition or a sponsor transaction, and all are executed and reported as completed except where marked as a subsequent event. On 2026-07-30 the issuer and a subsidiary borrower, Newell Brands Ireland Services DAC, with certain domestic and foreign subsidiary guarantors, entered a five-year asset-based revolving credit facility led by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. of up to 800, subject to a borrowing base of qualified cash, receivables, inventory, equipment and intellectual property, with an uncommitted accordion of up to 500; 490 was drawn on closing to repay and replace the 1,000 secured Credit Revolver that was due in August 2027. The facility is secured by a lien on deposit accounts, receivables, inventory, equipment and intellectual property, carries a Consolidated Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio test that applies only when borrowings exceed levels relative to capacity, and matures on 2031-07-30 or, if indebtedness of 125 or more is still outstanding 91 days before that debt's own scheduled maturity, on that 91st day before it. In August 2026 the issuer sold 600 of 6.250% senior unsecured notes due 2031 under an indenture dated 2026-08-19, received proceeds of 592, used them to redeem the 6.375% senior notes due 2027 at 101.530% (total consideration about 508) and to repay part of the ABL borrowings, and recorded a loss on extinguishment of 16 in Q3 2026 including 3 of revolver costs. At 2026-09-30, 215 was drawn on the ABL and letters of credit of 46 were issued under it, leaving net availability of about 480 on borrowing-base availability of 741; gross debt was 4,841 and net debt 4,592. The effect on liquidity is a longer runway and a clear 2027, but drawn secured borrowings now sit ahead of the unsecured notes in the same collateral pool as receivables and inventory, and, on the analyst's reading of the springing maturity (Analyst Interpretation), the facility's 2031 date holds only if the 2028 notes are refinanced or repaid in time; the 2028 notes' exact maturity date is not printed in the pages read.

The Customer Receivables Purchase Agreement limit was cut from 700 to 625 effective 2026-09-14, with a first-priority lien granted to the purchaser over certain receivables not sold and a lower funding rate; 300 was outstanding at 2026-09-30. The separate Receivables Facility, with 135 outstanding at 2026-09-30, was renewed effective 2026-10-02 (a subsequent event) to 2027-10-01 with its limit on factored receivables outstanding cut to 75. Management says it expects to reduce total debt and factoring by a couple of hundred million dollars in 2026 and that lower factoring proceeds reduce expected 2026 operating cash flow, now about 150; this is Management Language and is unproven. Earlier financings in the record: in May 2025 the issuer sold 1.25 billion of 8.500% senior notes due 2028 and used the proceeds to redeem its 4.200% notes due 2026 in June 2025, and in 2025 it repaid its 3.900% notes due 2025. No acquisition, divestiture or ownership change occurs in 2026 in the pack; the 2019 sale of The United States Playing Card Company is the source of a pending indemnification claim by the buyers, whose amount is not quantified. This module synthesises the fundamental credit view from the accepted financial base and business context, on the consolidated registrant in USD, with Q3 2026 as the current period and FY2025 as the prior period.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: NEWELL BRANDS INC. is a leveraged, turnaround-stage consumer brands credit that is improving but not yet self-funding. The strongest support is earnings momentum and liquidity: trailing-twelve-month normalized EBITDA is USD 1,030 million, net debt to that EBITDA is 4.46x at Q3 2026 against 5.07x at FY2025, the 2027 notes are redeemed, and liquidity is USD 729 million before factoring. The weakest point is cash conversion: operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 53 million over the last twelve months, well below net interest expense of USD 341 million and dividends of USD 127 million, and net debt rose by USD 122 million since FY2025. Outcomes turn on whether EBITDA gains become free cash flow and debt reduction before the USD 1,252 million 2028 notes fall due, since the new asset-based facility can mature earlier if they remain outstanding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Leverage improved on earnings, not repayment. NEWELL BRANDS INC. reports net debt of USD 4,592 million against USD 4,470 million at FY2025, so the fall in net debt to normalized EBITDA from 5.07x to 4.46x comes from trailing-twelve-month normalized EBITDA rising from USD 882 million to USD 1,030 million. That EBITDA is a management measure; it includes tariff recoveries recorded in Q2 2026, and removing the roughly USD 126 million named for that quarter would put net leverage near 5.08x (a one-sided sensitivity, calculated below). On a filing-based EBITDA before impairment the ratio is 5.51x. The issuer reported a GAAP net loss of USD 323 million over the twelve months to Q3 2026. Mechanic: lenders and the market will test sustainability of EBITDA, not the reported ratio. Implication: debt service capacity is thinner than the headline ratio suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Cash generation does not cover the obligations ahead of equity. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 53 million over the twelve months to Q3 2026, against net interest expense of USD 341 million and cash dividends of USD 127 million, leaving USD 74 million negative after dividends. First-quarter seasonality and an inventory build explain part of the profile, and Q3 2026 alone was strongly positive, but the year relies on the third and fourth quarters, and receivables factoring and tariff refunds have supported operating cash flow. Implication: refinancing, not internal cash, funds any maturity; the issuer's own full-year operating cash flow outlook of about USD 150 million is a management claim.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. The capital structure is pushed out but not de-risked. The USD 500 million 2027 notes are gone and the secured revolver was replaced by an asset-based facility of up to USD 800 million, with USD 215 million drawn and USD 480 million of net availability at 2026-09-30. The next large maturity is USD 1,252 million in 2028, which exceeds liquidity of USD 729 million before factoring. Under the facility's terms its maturity springs to 91 days before the earliest material debt maturity if USD 125 million or more is still outstanding, so the 2028 notes can pull the facility's maturity forward (the 2028 notes' exact date is not printed in the pages read). Implication: access to the bond market in 2027 and early 2028 is the decisive event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Priority claims on current assets are growing. The asset-based facility is secured on receivables, inventory, equipment, intellectual property and deposit accounts, and a receivables purchaser holds a first-priority lien on certain unsold receivables. At 2026-09-30 about USD 435 million of receivables were sold across two programs, and borrowing-base availability of USD 741 million means drawn secured borrowings could rise by USD 526 million from USD 215 million. Mechanic: more secured and sold claims on the same current assets reduce the unencumbered pool behind USD 4,626 million of other debt. This is a mechanic, not a recovery conclusion; lien priority between the lenders and the purchaser is not described in the pages read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Business risk is concentrated. Amazon and Walmart supplied about 17% and 13% of FY2025 net sales, the 10-K says retailer power may limit price recovery, Learning and Development earned more than the whole nine-month 2026 segment operating income while Home and Commercial Solutions earned USD 9 million, and a USD 101 million tradename impairment fell in Q3 2026. Implication: a retailer decision or a weak category can move cash flow materially, and impairments signal that asset values already reflect lower expected earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Debt-like funding sits outside the debt figure. Factoring of USD 435 million is not in reported debt; the issuer has cut both programs' limits and intends to reduce debt and factoring by a couple of hundred million dollars in 2026. Net debt plus factoring over normalized EBITDA is 4.88x (calculated below). Reducing factoring draws on liquidity unless replaced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. (1) Brand breadth and reach: the issuer sells in over 150 countries with a portfolio including Rubbermaid, Sharpie, Graco, Coleman and Yankee Candle (Documentary Fact). (2) Earnings momentum: trailing-twelve-month normalized EBITDA rose from USD 882 million at FY2025 to USD 1,030 million at Q3 2026, and management reports two consecutive quarters of sales growth (Documentary Fact for the figures; Management Language for the growth characterisation). (3) Maturity runway: the 2027 notes were redeemed and the asset-based facility runs to 2031 on its stated terms (Documentary Fact). (4) A profitable core: Learning and Development earned a segment operating income of USD 553 million over nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact). (5) Seasonal cash generation: Q3 2026 operating cash flow of USD 297 million, derived from cumulative statements, shows the model produces cash in the second half (Analyst Interpretation). (6) Transparent reporting with net debt and EBITDA reconciliations each quarter (Documentary Fact).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. (1) Leverage: net debt to normalized EBITDA of 4.46x, and 5.51x on a filing-based basis before impairment, with GAAP losses over the last twelve months (Documentary Fact and calculation). (2) Thin cash conversion relative to interest and dividends (Documentary Fact and calculation). (3) Customer concentration and weak pricing power (Documentary Fact). (4) A weak largest segment: Home and Commercial Solutions had a segment operating loss of USD 138 million in FY2025 and carries the Q3 2026 impairment, and Outdoor and Recreation lost USD 17 million over nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact). (5) Structural subordination risk through secured borrowing-base debt and sold receivables, and a springing maturity (Analyst Interpretation). (6) Reliance on management measures and one-off tariff refunds in 2026 earnings and cash flow (Documentary Fact). (7) Covenant headroom, ownership and ratings cannot be assessed from the pack (Insufficient Information; not an adverse conclusion).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The analysis of NEWELL BRANDS INC. is traceable enough for committee use on what it states, and restricted on what the pack cannot support. Every locator quoted in the four handoffs was found verbatim on its cited page, and every derived figure recomputes from the quoted inputs. The most important claims, leverage, cash conversion, liquidity and the 2028 refinancing, trace to filed statements or to management reconciliations that are labelled as management claims. The most important provenance gap is that leverage uses management's normalized EBITDA, with no covenant EBITDA and no add-back bridge to filed lines, while covenant levels, interim cash interest and ownership are not in the pack at all. One calculation in the synthesis is wrong and is corrected below; the earlier handoff cannot be edited.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. The credit synthesis (Key findings, item 4, and the calculation row for additional secured drawing capacity) states that drawn secured borrowings could rise by 526 from 215, computed as 741 - 215. That omits the 46 of letters of credit issued under the same facility, which also use availability. The correct additional drawing capacity is 741 - 215 - 46 = 480, which equals the net availability printed in the Q3 2026 report and used as liquidity in the financial base. The synthesis text should be read with 480 in place of 526; the mechanic it describes (more secured claims on current assets) is unchanged, and 480 also implies a smaller rise in the priority claim.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. The credit synthesis calls the 1,252 maturity bucket the 2028 notes. The 2025-12-31 maturity ladder prints 1,252 for 2028, which the 10-K supports as 1,250 of 8.500% notes plus other debt; the principal of the notes is 1,250. The difference is 2, does not change any ratio and is a labelling matter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. The business context tags the sector label as a Documentary Fact sourced to the run context. The run context is a settings file, not issuer evidence, so the label should be read as context-supplied and Not independently sourced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. The credit synthesis describes unsecured notes ranking behind the secured facility generally. Only the 2028 and 2031 notes are stated as senior unsecured obligations in the pages read; for the 2029, 2030, 2032, 2036 and 2046 notes the security is not printed there, and the rating agencies' references to senior unsecured debt are the only wording. The conclusion is plausible but its lineage is Weak for those series.
